text:
maria: Quick flag — after last night's KMS alias rotate (idp-encrypt-prod -> idp-encrypt-v2) a few tenants show duplicate service accounts created by SCIM. Not a mass outage but reproducible on two customer orgs.

kevin: Ugh. Are the duplicates for the same external_id or different? Any HTTP 4xx/5xx in the SCIM logs?

maria: Same displayName/email, different "externalId" (one has the old wrapped extid). SCIM logs show 409 on POST -> then we retry and create shadow account. Snip from scim-provisioner log for tenant-42:

```
2026-03-21T02:12:14Z INFO scim-provisioner attempt=1 tenant=tenant-42 POST /Users -> 409 Conflict {"detail":"externalId mismatch"}
2026-03-21T02:12:15Z WARN scim-provisioner retrying create after reconciliation
2026-03-21T02:12:16Z INFO scim-provisioner create /Users id=usr_abc123 (shadow)
2026-03-21T02:12:17Z ERROR kms-wrap decrypt failed: invalid JWE header alg RSA-OAEP (expected RSA-OAEP-256)
```

sam: That error looks like we still have tokens/wrapped IDs with the old OAEP alg encoding. During alias rotate we did a rewrap job but maybe it failed for tenants with long queues.

olivia: Did the rewrap job log tenant-level failures? I remember we skip on decrypt errors and leave original ciphertext to avoid bricking accounts.

maria: Right. It skipped and SCIM attempted to create a new account because our extId normalization compares decrypted extId -> null mismatch.

kevin: Two-pronged question: 1) how to fix duplicates without manual customer work, 2) how to avoid creating shadow accounts on reconciliation.

sam: For 1) we can run a backfill that attempts safe rewrap and then dedupe by email+displayName with a reconciliation transaction that prefers existing account if extId decrypt fails. Plan: decrypt with both algs (RSA-OAEP and RSA-OAEP-256) fallback, rewrap to current alias, and update extId field. If decryption fails for both, mark tenant for manual review.

olivia: For 2) change scim-provisioner reconcile flow: if create POST returns 409, do a stronger compare on email+entitlements before creating shadow, and add a circuit to avoid creating a new user if extId decryption fails — instead escalate to async worker.

maria: Quick checklist I ran: verified KMS alias mapping in vault, confirmed key policy allowed Decrypt for service principal, and confirmed rewrap job had a 0.3% failure rate (10 tenants).

kevin: Actions:
- sam to run the extended rewrap backfill targeting the 10 failed tenants and add alg fallback logic (ETA 4h)
- olivia to patch scim-provisioner reconcile to not create shadow accounts on extId-decrypt-failure (small release, ETA 2h)
- maria to open audit ticket + customer outreach for the 3 tenants with visible duplicates (I'll own comms)

idp-bot: Note: KMS alias rotate for idp-encrypt-prod completed 2026-03-21T01:05:00Z. Rewrap job started 2026-03-21T01:10:00Z -> finished 2026-03-21T01:58:23Z (10 failures).

sam: One more gotcha — RBAC role attachments are keyed by extId in downstream systems. If we dedupe by email, make sure we copy over role bindings from shadow to canonical account in the same reconciliation transaction to avoid entitlement loss.

maria: Good call. sam, include a migration step to merge role bindings and emit an audit log per merged user (tenant, old_extid, new_extid, roles). We'll need these for compliance.

kevin: Also add an alert to alerting: if scim-provisioner creates >1 shadow user for same email within 10m, page eng-security-ops.

olivia: I'll open the PR for the reconcile change and add tests for decrypt-failure path.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll update customer tickets after we confirm backfill success.

kevin: Thanks — ping here when sam has rewrap run results.

sam: Will do, kicking off now.
